body:
This PR adds a candidate, unrefereed upper-bound row **C82 < 0.252404806\* (rigorous, verify_interval.py)** to `constants/82a.md`, the README table line and Recent progress. It retains every existing row and credit. No global priority or optimality claim is made.

The construction starts from the public certificate of V. Patankar (@vidigoat) in PR #280 and the weighted-evaluation closest-vector method from #280, including Schnorr–Euchner enumeration and product starts. Of the six degree-104 denominator factors, four are new here; the other two, and all thirteen active numerators, are factors from #280's certificate (the numerators include Doche's P-factors and #301's MS192 and MS360). What this PR adds is those four denominators and the re-solved exact weights, which lower #280's 0.2524177045\* by about 1.29 × 10⁻⁵. It also reuses the reduced-cost formula, residue-class restriction and joint LP from our PR #301. Doche is credited for the limit-point construction, Grinsztajn for earlier factors and perturbative denominators, and Épi for earlier factors and unequal multiplicities, as on the live page.

The search imports two of V. Patankar's MIT-licensed files from vidigoat/optimization-records: `core.py` unchanged and `wlp.py` with one added thread setting. The licence and the file list are in the packet's [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICE.md](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICE.md). An earlier version of the packet said no vidigoat module was imported; that was wrong and is corrected there. Neither the interval verifier nor the referee's checker imports these files.

The certificate has six monic degree-104 denominator factors and thirteen active numerators. Computation supplies the interval enclosure of H+J, certified root isolation, and exact checks of integer coefficients, positive integer multiplicities, nonnegative rational exponents, the strict weighted-degree inequality and numerator/denominator coprimality. The fresh release replay checks all 78 active gcd pairs and 1644 composed roots; its exact upper endpoint passes the stated rational target. Floating search prices and the certificate's numeric_unverified field are not proof evidence.

The mathematical reduction is Doche's limit-point argument: C. Doche, [“Zhang-Zagier heights of perturbed polynomials”](https://www.numdam.org/item/JTNB_2001__13_1_103_0/), J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 13 (2001), 103–110, equations (5)–(9). The [proof](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/PROOF.md) writes out the referee's extraction step: each fixed algebraic number has bounded multiplicity in the growing polynomial family, so a finite set cannot absorb its limiting average height. This yields the essential-minimum bound, without asserting attainment at B. The theorem and extraction remain mathematical arguments requiring review; the computation encloses B and checks the finite hypotheses.

The release freshly reruns the separately written interval verifier on the frozen certificate on a local macOS machine, one process and one FLINT thread, in **18.40 seconds**. The [receipt](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/receipts/release-verifier.json) records exact dyadic endpoints and the certificate/source hashes. [REPRODUCE.md](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/REPRODUCE.md) gives both checker commands. Packaging does not repeat the heuristic search or the referee's complete control run.

**Referee.** A separate AI referee, given only the proof text and certificate and instructed to attack the claim, wrote its own complete interval checker and reproduced the bound. Verdict: **HOLDS WITH CAVEATS**. The input proof had the wrong Doche title and omitted the explicit extraction argument; the release proof corrects both, crediting the referee. Its [original proof input](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/review/inputs/PROOF.md) and [certificate input](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/review/inputs/certificates/certificate.json) remain byte-identical. The receipt's exact model string is preserved: “GPT-6-based Codex (exact serving-model ID not exposed)”. According to the launcher record, the referee ran on GPT-6 Astra; the receipt itself cannot establish that identity or the model difference. This is an AI review, not a second human party.

**Verification level: L0** for the bound as a whole (definitions: https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/59eeb7097f806da05187b5f234445be3589204d4/VERIFICATION_LEVELS.md)
The search and verifier were written by the same AI agent. A separate AI referee, launched on a different model according to the launcher record (not attested by its receipt), reproduced the bound from the proof text and certificate alone (HOLDS WITH CAVEATS: the cited Doche title was wrong in its input; its exact model ID is not exposed).

Supporting material: [packet](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/tree/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp), [certificate](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/certificate.json), [numerical enclosure method](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/NUMERICS.md), [search method](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/METHOD.md), [verifier](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/verify_interval.py), [referee report](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/review/REFEREE.md), [replay receipt (input paths re-rooted to this packet, same hashes)](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/REPLAY.json), [source audit](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/PRIOR_ART.md) and [third-party notice](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/5461d490552a518667c3fd3fceff33ebdb4d347c/c82/degree104-cvp/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICE.md). Certificate artifacts belong in math-certificates; the optimizationproblems diff contains only the two Markdown updates.

The live merged page prints 0.2536331090204145 (0.2534449\*, unrefereed) as the upper entry ([cited table row](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/blob/87b4ebbd426ff8db597a2004cc45da17903bdcf2/constants/82a.md)). The pending #280 bound is 0.2524177045\* ([cited PR](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/280)); the pending #301 bound is 0.253091834\* ([cited PR](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/301)). The source refresh on 4 November 2026 found #242, #280 and #301 as the only open PRs changing 82a. This patch applies on main and adds only its own row. If #280 or #301 merges first, retain their historical rows and references and append this candidate; in the shared README line, keep the existing lower entry and unasterisked upper value and replace only the parenthesized candidate with this PR's value. #242 changes the asterisks on older rows and also rewrites the README 82 cell to `0.24874 | 0.2534449`; if #242 merges first, the upper cell becomes 0.2534449 (0.252404806\*), keeping its replay records. No claim is made that these open PRs have merged. The public-source check is scoped, not an exhaustive priority finding.

AI use and author review: Analysis and proof drafting by AI agents under my direction; I reviewed the results at summary level. AI agents also prepared the certificate, verifiers and submission text. This does not claim a line-by-line human verification.

**Models:** GPT-6.1 Sol via Codex (search, proof drafting, certificate, verifier, packaging); GPT-6 Astra via Codex, per the launcher record (separate AI referee and replay); Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 (coordination and PR-text revisions).
